title: Brač Prices and Realistic Budget for 2027
metaDescription: How Brač prices have changed and what to budget in 2027: ferries, apartments, konoba meals, car hire and daily costs, with insider savings tips.
content:
## How Much Does Brač Cost in 2027?

Brač is a mid-priced Croatian island. Prices are lower than on Hvar, but higher than the mainland interior. The 2027 budget below is built on 2026 price levels plus a modest allowance for increases. Croatia has been on the euro since 2023, and the rise in tourist prices since then has been well documented. Croatia is now seen as the most expensive country in the Western Balkans.

Planning figures per person per day, excluding flights:

- **Budget:** €60–90 (self-catering, a simple room or hostel, one restaurant meal, buses)
- **Mid-range:** €110–180 (apartment or 3-star hotel, two restaurant meals, a rental scooter or car some days)
- **Luxury:** €250–400+ (boutique hotel or villa, fine dining, boat trips)

For 2027, add roughly 3–6% to accommodation and restaurant prices. Ferry fares are set annually, so 2027 tariffs were not confirmed at the time of writing.

## How Have Prices in Brač Changed Recently?

Three trends stand out:

1. **Restaurants and accommodation rose fastest.** Hotels and restaurants in Croatia sit at about 95% of the EU average. Food and non-alcoholic drinks are now slightly above it.
2. **Ferry fares stayed stable.** The standard Split–Supetar adult fare is €6.50 for the whole of 2026. This is one of the few costs that has barely moved.
3. **Seasonal spreads widened.** July and August rates for apartments and villas can be double those of May, June or late September.

The practical effect: when you travel matters more than which town you choose.

## Ferry and Transport Costs to Brač

### Split to Supetar by ferry

Jadrolinija line 631 runs Split to Supetar in about 50 minutes. The adult one-way fare is €6.50 and a child aged 3–12 pays €3.20. Children under 3 travel free.

Vehicle fares are charged separately:

- Motorcycle or scooter: €12.90
- Car up to 5 m: €26.10
- Large car (over 5 m or 2 m high): €40.30
- Camper up to 5 m: €42.90

A car with two adults therefore costs about €39 one way, or €78 return.

### Krilo catamaran

The Kapetan Luka (Krilo) catamaran takes about 20 minutes from Split to Supetar and costs €10.00 per person one way. It runs roughly every two hours in the day, with departures from Split around 06:25, 08:00, 10:00, 12:00, 14:00, 16:00 and 18:00. It carries no cars.

### Split to Milna

High-speed passenger services also run to Milna on the west coast. Fares start around €6–7 in the cheaper options. Milna suits visitors staying in the west or heading to Bol by road.

### Getting around the island

Buses link Supetar with Bol, Milna and Postira, but frequency drops sharply outside summer. Supetar to Bol is about 45 km by road. A scooter costs about €30–50 per day and a small car €40–70 per day, with fuel around €1.50–1.65 per litre. A car is worth it for a stay of three days or more.

**Insider tip:** Walk on and rent a scooter or car on the island if you stay under three days. Taking a car over costs €26.10 each way and often exceeds the cost of a rental.

## Accommodation Prices by Style

| Type | 2027 planning range (per night) |
| --- | --- |
| Hostel bed or basic room | €40–80 |
| 3-star hotel or good apartment | €100–180 |
| Villa with pool or boutique hotel | €250–800+ |

Bol, home of the Zlatni Rat beach, is the most expensive base. Supetar has the widest choice and the best ferry access. Milna, Postira and Sumartin tend to be cheaper and quieter. Private apartments make up most of the stock, and a two-person apartment in a smaller village in June or September often costs €60–90.

**Opinion:** For most travellers, Supetar is the best-value base. It offers ferry arrivals, supermarkets, beaches and bus links without Bol's premium.

## Food and Drink Prices

- Bakery breakfast and coffee: €5–8
- Pizza or simple lunch: €8–14
- Konoba main dish: €12–20
- Two-course dinner with wine: €25–40 per person
- Cheap restaurant meal: about €11
- Mid-range dinner for two: about €60
- Fine dining tasting menus in Croatia: about €95–160

Brač is known for lamb, peka (food slow-cooked under a bell-shaped lid), and Brač olive oil. Peka usually needs ordering several hours ahead and is priced for sharing. Self-catering is the easiest way to cut costs, since supermarkets in Supetar, Bol and Milna sell fresh fish, bread and produce at mainland prices.

**Insider tip:** Lunch menus and daily specials often cost less than dinner for the same dishes. Eat the main meal at midday.

## Sample 2027 Budgets

### One week, budget traveller (solo)

Roughly €420–630. This covers a hostel or room at €40–60, a return ferry at €13, self-catered meals and occasional buses.

### One week, mid-range couple

Roughly €1,500–2,400 in total. This includes an apartment or hotel at €100–180 per night, meals of €60–100 per day for two, ferry fares and a three-day car rental.

### Long weekend, luxury

Around €250–400 per person per day. This covers a boutique hotel in Bol, fine dining and a private boat trip.

## Best Time to Visit for Lower Prices

Late May, June and September give warm sea temperatures with lower accommodation prices than July and August. October is cheaper still but several seasonal restaurants and rental firms close. Ferry timetables are also thinner in winter. Book summer stays early, because mid-range apartments and hotels sell out well ahead.

## Money-Saving Tips

- **Book the cheaper ferry for the schedule you need.** The Jadrolinija ferry is €3.50 cheaper than the catamaran but takes 30 minutes longer.
- **Buy catamaran tickets online or at the Krilo kiosk** at Split port to avoid queues.
- **Avoid beachfront restaurants** at Zlatni Rat for main meals. Prices run higher than in the town centre.
- **Shop at supermarkets** for picnic lunches. They cost a quarter of a beach café meal.
- **Travel mid-week** where possible. Weekend ferry queues for vehicles are long in July and August.

## Is Brač Worth the Cost?

Yes, for most budgets. It combines easy access from Split, many beaches and a wide range of accommodation. It costs less than Hvar and is far easier to reach than the outer islands. The main risk is peak-season pricing, which is avoidable by travelling in June or September.

faq.question: How much does a day in Brač cost in 2027?
faq.answer: Budget travellers should plan €60–90 per person per day, mid-range travellers €110–180, and luxury travellers €250 or more. Accommodation and the time of year have the largest effect on the total.

faq.question: How much is the ferry from Split to Brač?
faq.answer: The Jadrolinija car ferry to Supetar costs €6.50 for an adult one way and takes about 50 minutes. The Krilo catamaran costs €10.00 and takes about 20 minutes. A car adds €26.10 each way on the Jadrolinija ferry.

faq.question: Is Brač cheaper than Hvar?
faq.answer: Yes. Brač has more private apartments and more villages away from the main resorts, so there are more mid-priced options. Bol is the priciest part of Brač, but still generally cheaper than Hvar Town in summer.

faq.question: Do I need a car on Brač?
faq.answer: A car or scooter helps for stays of three days or more, because buses are infrequent outside summer. Rental costs about €40–70 per day for a car and €30–50 for a scooter. For short stays, renting on the island is usually cheaper than shipping a car over.

faq.question: How much does dinner cost in Brač?
faq.answer: A konoba main dish is usually €12–20. A two-course dinner with wine runs about €25–40 per person. Pizza and simple lunches cost €8–14.

faq.question: When is the cheapest time to visit Brač?
faq.answer: Late May, June and September offer good weather and lower accommodation prices than July and August. Outside these months, many restaurants and rental firms close, so choice is limited.

faq.question: Will Brač prices rise in 2027?
faq.answer: A moderate rise of about 3–6% in accommodation and restaurant prices is a sensible planning assumption. Ferry fares are set yearly, and the 2026 adult fare of €6.50 had not been updated for 2027 at the time of writing.

quickAnswer: A realistic 2027 budget for Brač is about €60–90 per person per day on a budget, €110–180 mid-range, and €250+ for luxury. Ferries from Split cost €6.50 for foot passengers. Accommodation is the biggest variable, and July–August prices run far above shoulder-season rates.
